newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - APRIL 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - APRIL 14.

text.p: AUSTRIA
DER STANDARD
- Currently two petitions, one against gene-manipulation and the other for women's rights, are about to become the most successful in the country's history.
- Maria Rauch-Kallat, general secretary of the conservative People's Party, wants to open the party for more liberal minded voters.
- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl is thinking of changing parts of the new foreigner law, as criticism of the harsh law is strong.
- The U.S. secret service CIA bugged into rooms of a Vienna hotel to listen in on OPEC delegations from Iran and Iraq.

- Austria's largest builder Bau Holding is expanding abroad to compensate for the bad economic situation at home. Now the company received an order to build 250 million schillings worth of motorway in Italy

- Motor engineer Steyr-Daimler-Puch sees chances in Asia to improve the business. The company plans to offer engineering to Indian and Chinese companies while talks with South Korea's car maker Hyundai are also on the way.
DIE PRESSE
- Chancellor Viktor Klima says work hour reduction will only be done by reducing the wages too.

- The Transport Ministry has only found one bidder for Austria's third mobile phone network. Connect, the only interested party, sees massive start hinderances to be the reason for this lack of offers. The ministry still hopes to receive at least three offers.

- Bawag bank and insurer EA-Generali expected to jointly bid for the government's stake in postal savings bank PSK. Insurer Wiener Staedtische is now seen not to want to make an offer for tha bank together with insurance holding BARC.
KURIER
- Civil servants plan to resist against plans by the government to continue the austerity measures in the civil service, as Klima wants to strongly reduce the number of employees.
- Chamber of Labour chief Werner Muhm demands Unilever expand production in Austria should it go ahead with the closure of one production facility as profits are very high anyway.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV plans to restart a project to supply Italy with gas via Croatia.
- Bank Austria plans to merge its foreign activities with Creditanstalt's, which it took over in January.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Swiss pharmaceuticals group Hoffmann La-Roche wil create 150 jobs by investing two billion schillings in its research facility in northern Austria.
BULGARIA
24 CHASA
-- Bulgaria's exiled king Simeon II is expected to arrive in the country tomorrow, the king'g presscentre said.
The visit is related to the 118 aniversary of the approval of the first Bulgarian constitution.
-- Bulgaria is expected to sell six state owned banks by the year-end, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Bulgaria expects to receive $22.5 million from Russia under an accord for the reconstruction of Bulgaria's neuclear power plant Kosloduy reactors, an energy expert said.
TRUD

-- Bulgaria is expected to introduce compulsory AIDS test for all visiting foreigners who would stay more than one month in the country in a bid to tighten the spread of the disease, a Health ministry senior official said.
-- Bulgaria's prime minister Stefan Sofianski is expected to leave for Moscow today.
Sofianski is expected to meet with his Russian counterpart Viktor Chernomirdin in a bid to boost the bilatteral cooperation.
PARI
-- Bulgaria has received $19 million from its international lenders to finilise the restoration of private ownership on the arable land, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said.
-- Bulgaria's interim government is expected to discuss today the possible sale of a 75 percent stake in Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
STANDART
-- Bulgaria's foreign minister Stoyan Stalev is expected to leave for Greece today.
Stalev is expected to meet with his Greek counterpart Teodoros Pangalos in a bid to boost Greek investments in Bulgaria.
-- The US General Electric is interested to buy Bulgaria's state Varna coal power station, an energy expert said.
ESTONIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- The security police are concerned with the traffic of narcotics, radioactive substances and weapons, police chief Juri Pihl said at a security forum on Saturday. He described corruption among Russian state officials and international crime as the greatest threat to Estonia.
SONUMILEHT
- A poll conducted by Tartu students shows that 66 percent of the residents of the town want former mayor Tonu Lukas to continue.

- The prime minister's ethnic affairs advisor Yevgeni Golikov will prepare a report on the crisis at the northeastern peat plant of Oru after the workers of the bankrupt plant presented their political demands.
- A longer article discusses the deteriorating reputation of the state among the citizens and the inadequate PR work of government institutions.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- Savings Bank, Hansapank and Uhispank held their shareholders meetings Saturday. Only Hansapank paid dividends.

- Organisers announced only a limited number of tickets for the Michael Jackson concert will be sold. The initial price of 390 kroons will gradually rise to 490 and 590 kroons unless the tickets are sold out at once. The sale will begin on April 22.
- EU Commissioner Hans van den Broek is to arrive for a visit to Estonia today.
POSTIMEES
- The prime minister's Mercedes-Benz E-420 official car was damaged in a slight collision with a security escort vehicle on Saturday.
ARIPAEV
- The furniture and ski producer "Viisnurk" will issue in May 90,000 new shares worth 11.7 million kroons.
- The Estline shipping firm plans to introduce a new RO-RO ferry this summer and a passenger ship next year.
LATVIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- The leader of the Fatherland & Freedom party, Maris Griblats, announced that a compromise on choosing two of the privatisation agency's directors through an open competition is nothing but avoiding transparency in the privatisation process and making it only partly democratic.
- There was a military review in Liepaja on April 12, devoted to the fifth anniversary of Latvian navy forces. The navy has 17 warships, of which two are mine sweepers.
- President Guntis Ulmanis arrived in France on a two-day official visit, whose goal is to draw attention to security issues in the Baltic region.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs anounced on his return from a central Asian tour that his visit was a success. He said that Latvia, Russia and Uzbekistan may create a joint work group to expanding the transit corridor and make it safer. Around 1/3 of Uzbekistan's cotton exports goes through Latvian harbours.
BIZNES & BALTIJA
- Beginning today, shares of Latvia's Savings Bank will be available in public auction.
SM
- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs announced at a press-conference that Latvia is ready to sign a border treaty with Russia at any time.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- Finance Minister Roberts Zile said in an interview that he believes tax rates in Latvia are at a normal level except for social tax. The minister regards free economic zones as one of instruments to increase the country's GDP.
- The state revenue service plans to invest 22.7 million lats over the five coming years to increase the state income.
